artifacts.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

artifacts.title: Brian Abshire v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC largely denied TE Abshire's complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, finding that the Presbytery did not err in appointing a judicial commission or issuing a pastoral exhortation, but sustained the error in the commission's ruling on Lynch and Rooney's complaint without following BCO 43 procedures, remanding that specific matter to Presbytery.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the complaint, finding that the Session of Faith Presbyterian Church failed to follow BCO 38-4 procedures when it attempted to retroactively erase Carolyn Goerig's membership after banning her from attending services, and that the Presbytery erred in denying her complaint. Because her membership transfer to another church was never completed, she remained under Faith PC's jurisdiction per BCO 46-3.
